list.title: 1. Restriction Enzyme Digestion:
list.snippet: The first step involves using a restriction enzyme to precisely cut the gene from its source DNA. Restriction enzymes recognize specific DNA sequences and cut the DNA at those sites, creating DNA fragments with "sticky ends" or "blunt ends".

list.title: 2. Preparing the Vector:
list.snippet: The cloning vector (usually a plasmid) also needs to be cut with the same restriction enzyme to create compatible ends. This allows the gene to be inserted into the plasmid.

list.title: 3. Joining the Fragments:
list.snippet: The cut gene fragment and the cut plasmid are then mixed together. The complementary ends of the DNA fragments will naturally anneal (stick together).

list.title: 4. Ligation:
list.snippet: Finally, DNA ligase is used to covalently bond the gene to the plasmid, creating a recombinant DNA molecule.

text_blocks.snippet: This process allows the gene to be inserted into the plasmid and then introduced into a bacterial cell where it can be replicated and expressed.
